reason: Conversation 1 keeps to UK-appropriate power checks (spur switch, consumer unit, fuse swap with power off) and never commits to a failed part. It explains how to open the spur fuse holder and escalates to an engineer if a fresh fuse changes nothing. Conversation 2 opens with US advice (GFCI outlets, a wall switch near the disposal) and then asserts that the control or power module is 'the most common cause' with a £100-200 price. It also says the fuse is 'almost certainly fine' and that 'power is reaching it', which the evidence does not establish, and that makes it overconfident and part-naming. Conversation 2 does usefully get the model number and notes the Neff door-edge display, but its unsupported diagnosis outweighs that.
